title: Który · przez przypadki
note:
B1 Block 6 opener. Opens complex sentences: który stops being just the a2_questions2 interrogative ('which film?', Nominative, subject position only) and becomes a real RELATIVE pronoun connecting two clauses ('the film THAT I was watching'). This is genuinely one new idea — który's CASE is set by its job inside its OWN clause, not by the noun it refers back to (which stays whatever case the main clause needs, unmarked) — demonstrated on the two case values the spine names: Accusative (książka, którą czytałem — czytać is a plain transitive verb, already known to take an accusative object) and Genitive (film, którego nie ma — nie ma is the already-known existential-negation pattern that always takes genitive, a1_negation). Both cases are motivated by verbs/patterns the learner already owns; the only new thing is that który itself now carries that case.

SCOPE CUT, logged (spine: 'Loc/Inst relatives deferred within B1 or fenced — author's conservative call'): Locative and Instrumental relatives (o którym myślę, z którym mieszkam) are NOT in this unit. Fenced completely — not shown, not hinted, not a distractor string anywhere. Left for a later B1 pass or a dedicated case_gym-style unit; not on the current B1-SPINE as its own slot.

SECOND SCOPE CUT, logged: antecedents are restricted to INANIMATE/ABSTRACT nouns only (książka, film, wino, kawa, list) in both the Accusative and Genitive tables. Masculine-ANIMATE antecedents (pies, brat, kolega) would merge Accusative with Genitive on the noun itself — a real, already-known rule (AGENTS.md's 'honest exception': brata/psa/kota identical in Acc and Gen) — but bringing that in here means the masculine relative pronoun would need to look like Gen ("którego") for animate antecedents in the ACCUSATIVE table too, for a different reason than the Genitive table's którego. Stacking two unrelated reasons for the same surface form in one unit was judged the wrong trade for an absolute beginner's first relative-clause unit; conservative call is inanimate-only, animate relatives deferred (most likely a gym or a small follow-up), flagged for James.

HOMOGRAPH, confirmed via check_new.py before writing a single line, exactly the shape AGENTS.md's table warns about: której already sits in POOL, taught by a2_ordinals_time — but frozen inside the chunk o której? ('at what time'), never explained as a case, never contrasted with anything. This is the SAME underlying grammatical fact (feminine genitive of który) the learner has been saying by rote since A2, now generalised into a real, productive case form for the first time. Treated like b1_dative_sg treated dziękuję (chunk -> real paradigm slot), not like the ci/ci pair (two unrelated words) — the intro names the connection explicitly rather than pretending the string is brand new. który and które are re-listed in teaches_lemmas too, for the same reason ci was in b1_dative_pron: same string, genuinely new FUNCTION (relative pronoun, not interrogative) — logged rather than silently assumed identical.

6 teaches_lemmas: którą (fem Acc, genuinely new form), którego (masc/neut Gen, genuinely new form), której (re-taught, see above), który + które (re-taught for the new relative function, same strings as a2_questions2's interrogative), oglądałem (past tense of the already-present-tense-known verb oglądać, applying the already-owned past_ac rule to a new lemma — not new grammar). Every other word in every example (czytałem/czytałam, piłem, nie ma, film, książka, wino, kawa, list) confirmed already taught via check_new.py, listed in uses_lemmas, recycled untouched.

intro.title: Który becomes a real word: relative clauses
intro.body:
You already know który as a question word: Który film? (Which film?) — always in subject position, always Nominative. From here, który does something new: it joins two sentences into one, meaning "that" or "which".

To jest książka. Czytałem ją. → To jest książka, którą czytałem. (This is the book that I was reading.)

The key rule: który agrees in GENDER with the noun it points back to (like ten/ta/to), but its CASE comes from its own job inside its own little clause — completely separate from whatever case the main sentence needs.
intro.body_pl: który = "that/which" — łączy dwa zdania w jedno. Rodzaj = jak rzeczownik. Przypadek = jak jego rola we własnym zdaniu.

intro.title: Accusative relative: the verb inside decides
intro.body: czytać, oglądać and pić are plain transitive verbs — you have always given them a direct object in the accusative (Czytam książkę). Put one of them inside a który-clause and który itself takes that same accusative job, agreeing in gender with the noun it refers to.
intro.body_pl: książka (f) → którą. film (m, nieżywotny) → który, tak jak Nominative. wino (n) → które, tak jak Nominative.

examples.en: This is the book that I was reading.
This is the film that I was watching.
This is the wine that I was drinking.

intro.title: Genitive relative: nie ma decides
intro.body: You have known since your very first unit that nie ma always takes the genitive (Nie ma domu). That rule doesn't change here — it just now reaches into a który-clause too. Genitive który: masculine and neuter both look like którego; feminine is której.
intro.body_pl: nie ma + dopełniacz (bez zmian). film (m) → którego. wino (n) → którego (tak samo). kawa (f) → której.

intro.title: You already said której — just never like this
intro.body: Since A2 you have asked O której? — "At what time?". That której is this exact same word: the feminine genitive of który. It was frozen as a fixed phrase back then, with no explanation. Now you are learning it as a real, reusable case form — the same word, doing the same grammatical job, just no longer locked inside one fixed question.
intro.body_pl: O której? (już Twoje) = ta sama której, teraz jako prawdziwy przypadek, nie tylko zwrot.

match.en: that (masculine inanimate, accusative — same as which)
the book that I was reading
the film that I was watching
the wine that I was drinking
the book that I was reading (said by a woman)

quiz.prompt: The book that I was reading. →
quiz.explain: książka is feminine and is the object of czytałem inside its own clause — feminine accusative, którą.

quiz.prompt: The film that I was watching. →
quiz.explain: film is masculine inanimate — accusative looks exactly like Nominative here, który, the same as with any inanimate object.

quiz.prompt: The wine that I was drinking. →
quiz.explain: wino is neuter — accusative = Nominative, które, the same shape you already know.
nie ma always takes genitive (nie ma domu) — który follows the same rule here: masculine genitive, którego.
You already say o której (at what time) — this is that exact feminine genitive form, now doing the same job after nie ma.
Neuter and masculine share the same genitive ending here: którego, exactly like film above.
Masculine genitive: którego, forced by nie ma.
Feminine genitive: której — the same word as o której, doing a new job.

quiz.prompt: The letter that I was reading. →
quiz.explain: list is masculine inanimate, same pattern as film: accusative looks like Nominative, który.

type_items.explain: The same word you already know from o której? (at what time) — now a real, reusable case form.
Same string as the question word który — but here it is a relative pronoun, not a question.
